item.title: Warm, Sunny Weather Continues Through Thursday in Escambia County
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Escambia County area is tracking a pleasant stretch of weather before a weekend cool front moves in. Wednesday will be sunny with highs near 88 degrees and calm winds. Overnight, conditions remain clear with lows dropping to around 63. Thursday follows a similar pattern, with partly sunny skies gradually becoming sunny and highs near 86…
item.content:encoded:
The Escambia County area is tracking a pleasant stretch of weather before a weekend cool front moves in. Wednesday will be sunny with highs near 88 degrees and calm winds. Overnight, conditions remain clear with lows dropping to around 63.

Thursday follows a similar pattern, with partly sunny skies gradually becoming sunny and highs near 86 degrees. A light east wind around 5 mph is expected to develop. Thursday night will be mostly clear with lows again near 63.

The calm, dry conditions should make for comfortable outdoor activities, but residents should monitor forecasts for the cool front expected to arrive over the weekend.

item.title: Mysterious glowing plume lights up North Escambia skies before dawn
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Early risers across North Escambia got an unusual treat Tuesday morning when a glowing, iridescent plume swept across the eastern horizon in the predawn hours, according to local reports. The luminous display, which some observers described as resembling a giant jellyfish in space, was visible across the northern part of the county. Such phenomena…
item.content:encoded:
Early risers across North Escambia got an unusual treat Tuesday morning when a glowing, iridescent plume swept across the eastern horizon in the predawn hours, according to local reports.

The luminous display, which some observers described as resembling a giant jellyfish in space, was visible across the northern part of the county. Such phenomena are typically caused by rocket launches or debris reflecting sunlight at high altitude during twilight hours, when the sun illuminates objects in space while the ground remains dark.

No official confirmation has been released yet regarding the source of Tuesday's display. Anyone who witnessed the event is encouraged to report details to local authorities or astronomical groups who track such occurrences.

item.title: Visiting FFA Chapters Serve 700+ Meals to Storm-Hit Tate High Area
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Two Florida FFA chapters rolled into the Tate High School area Tuesday with more than 700 hot meals, bringing comfort and fellowship to neighbors still recovering from recent storm damage in North Escambia County. The visiting agricultural students demonstrated the kind of cross-county solidarity that defines rural community response — showing up…
item.content:encoded:
Two Florida FFA chapters rolled into the Tate High School area Tuesday with more than 700 hot meals, bringing comfort and fellowship to neighbors still recovering from recent storm damage in North Escambia County.

The visiting agricultural students demonstrated the kind of cross-county solidarity that defines rural community response — showing up with food, labor, and a commitment to helping their peers rebuild. The effort underscores how young people in agriculture-focused programs see disaster recovery not as someone else's problem, but as a shared responsibility.

Tate High School and the surrounding Gonzalez area have been dealing with storm aftermath, and meals like these do more than fill bellies; they give families breathing room to focus on cleanup and repairs without worrying about cooking. The FFA chapters' willingness to travel and serve signals that mutual aid networks in Northwest Florida extend well beyond single counties when disaster strikes.

item.title: Hurricane Relief Event Set for Molino Wednesday Morning
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Residents in north Escambia County affected by Hurricane Isaias can access emergency support services Wednesday morning in Molino. The relief event begins at 9 a.m. at CrossFaith Church, 5701 Highway 29, and is being organized in partnership with ECUA Board Member Kevin Stephens and local volunteers. The event will offer shower pods and restroom…
item.content:encoded:
Residents in north Escambia County affected by Hurricane Isaias can access emergency support services Wednesday morning in Molino. The relief event begins at 9 a.m. at CrossFaith Church, 5701 Highway 29, and is being organized in partnership with ECUA Board Member Kevin Stephens and local volunteers.

The event will offer shower pods and restroom facilities for residents without utilities, along with charging stations to power phones and devices. Free supplies will include meals ready to eat (MREs), bottled water, cleaning supplies, and hygiene kits — all available while supplies last.

This is one of several relief initiatives underway across Escambia County as recovery efforts continue in the aftermath of the hurricane.

item.title: Santa Rosa County Schools Extended Closed Through Oct. 19 After Storm Damage

The decision comes after severe weather impacted the county, prompting the board to keep facilities shuttered beyond initial closure dates. Teachers and parents raised…
item.content:encoded:
The Santa Rosa County School Board has extended school closures through October 19 due to storm damage and safety concerns, according to a report from Citizen Portal News Florida.

The decision comes after severe weather impacted the county, prompting the board to keep facilities shuttered beyond initial closure dates. Teachers and parents raised safety concerns that factored into the board's determination to maintain the closure.

No specific details on the extent of storm damage or which facilities were most heavily affected were immediately available. The closure affects all Santa Rosa County schools during the extended period.

The owner said he was fortunate to escape and attributes his survival to an officer who was on patrol in the area at…
item.content:encoded:
A Gulf Shores business was destroyed in a fire early Tuesday morning, but the owner credits a nearby police officer with saving his life.

According to WKRG News 5, the fire broke out before dawn and quickly consumed the structure. The owner said he was fortunate to escape and attributes his survival to an officer who was on patrol in the area at the time.

Details about the cause of the fire, the specific business, and the extent of the officer's intervention were not immediately disclosed. Authorities have not yet released a damage estimate or indicated whether an investigation into the fire's origin is underway.

item.content:encoded:
The Florida Department of Health in Okaloosa County is urging residents and visitors to stay out of beach water and public pools due to an increased risk of waterborne illness, according to WKRG-TV.

The advisory applies to both ocean and pool environments in the county. Health officials have not yet released specific details about the nature of the illness or the exact locations affected, but the warning suggests a situation serious enough to warrant public precaution.

Okaloosa County residents should monitor updates from the Florida Department of Health for more information on the duration of the warning and when it may be safe to resume normal water activities.

item.title: Escambia County cancels remaining 2026 neighborhood cleanups to focus on Hurricane Isaias recovery
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Escambia County Neighborhood and Human Services has suspended all remaining neighborhood cleanup events this year as the department redirects resources toward Hurricane Isaias cleanup and recovery efforts throughout the county. Four scheduled cleanups have been canceled: Navy Point/Beach Haven on October 14, Northpointe on October 21, Olive Road…
item.content:encoded:
Escambia County Neighborhood and Human Services has suspended all remaining neighborhood cleanup events this year as the department redirects resources toward Hurricane Isaias cleanup and recovery efforts throughout the county.

Four scheduled cleanups have been canceled: Navy Point/Beach Haven on October 14, Northpointe on October 21, Olive Road on November 4, and Ensley North on November 18. The county said neighborhood cleanup programs will resume in 2027, with updates to be posted on MyEscambia.com.

Meanwhile, Escambia County is preparing to begin collection of storm-generated debris from Hurricane Isaias later this week. Residents should note that commercial debris will not be included in the county's pickup service. More information about the debris collection program is available on the county's website.

item.title: ECAT Resumes Service Wednesday With Route Changes Due to Storm Debris
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Escambia County Area Transit will bring buses back on the road Wednesday, Oct. 14, but riders should expect some adjustments as crews work to clear storm debris from local streets. ECAT will operate normal service from 6 a.m. to 6 p.m., with FlexTransit running 5 a.m. to 8 p.m. However, Route 48 will not run at all due to impassable road…
item.content:encoded:
Escambia County Area Transit will bring buses back on the road Wednesday, Oct. 14, but riders should expect some adjustments as crews work to clear storm debris from local streets.

ECAT will operate normal service from 6 a.m. to 6 p.m., with FlexTransit running 5 a.m. to 8 p.m. However, Route 48 will not run at all due to impassable road conditions. On Route 51, Ensley Street will be skipped; riders needing that stop should board at Johnson Avenue and Vickie Street instead. The UWF trolleys also won't operate.

County officials warn that delays are likely across the system as cleanup continues. Commuters are advised to build extra time into their schedules. For questions, call ECAT at 850-595-3228.

item.content:encoded:
Four major roads in Okaloosa County will temporarily shut down this week as Eglin Air Force Base conducts scheduled testing and training operations, according to a news release from the base.

Highway 85, Highway 285, State Road 123, and Florida State Road 293 are all on the closure list. While the exact duration of the closures wasn't detailed in the available information, the military typically coordinates such road shutdowns to minimize traffic disruption during daylight hours when possible.

Drivers in Okaloosa County should plan alternate routes if they regularly use those corridors. Eglin periodically notifies the public about training activities that may impact local traffic, and residents can check the base's website or local traffic alerts for real-time updates on reopening times.

item.title: USPS Restores Most Northern Florida Services After Hurricane Isaias
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The U.S. Postal Service has restored operations at most facilities across Northern Florida following Hurricane Isaias, though a handful of locations remain temporarily shuttered, the agency announced today. Seven postal facilities in the region continue to have retail services suspended as cleanup and safety assessments continue. In the Pensacola…
item.content:encoded:
The U.S. Postal Service has restored operations at most facilities across Northern Florida following Hurricane Isaias, though a handful of locations remain temporarily shuttered, the agency announced today.

Seven postal facilities in the region continue to have retail services suspended as cleanup and safety assessments continue. In the Pensacola area, the Nobles branch at 7150 Tippin Avenue remains closed. Milton, Gonzalez, Shalimar, and Valparaiso locations are also affected, with no alternate sites currently available to customers in those ZIP codes.

The Postal Service said it is working to restore full operations as quickly and safely as possible at the remaining closed facilities. Customers can check for updated service alerts at about.usps.com/newsroom/service-alerts/.

item.title: DeSantis awards $27M to 14 rural Florida communities, including Panhandle counties
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Governor Ron DeSantis announced $27 million in infrastructure funding Tuesday to 14 small and rural communities across Florida, with eight of those awards going to Panhandle counties still recovering from Hurricane Isaias. The awards come through the Rural Infrastructure Fund, a state program supporting infrastructure projects that drive job…
item.content:encoded:
Governor Ron DeSantis announced $27 million in infrastructure funding Tuesday to 14 small and rural communities across Florida, with eight of those awards going to Panhandle counties still recovering from Hurricane Isaias.

The awards come through the Rural Infrastructure Fund, a state program supporting infrastructure projects that drive job creation and economic development in rural areas. According to the Governor's Press Office, the funding will support projects ranging from roadway connectivity improvements to stormwater infrastructure upgrades and building renovations.

Calhoun County is among the recipients, receiving nearly $2.5 million to acquire and renovate a commercial building next to the new Calhoun Liberty Hospital. The project will house a primary care clinic, rural specialty care center, and county EMS operations, and is expected to create about 33 full-time jobs. The Town of Century also received nearly $500,000 through the Florida Job Growth Grant Fund for a building renovation and fire suppression system upgrade.

FloridaCommerce received 141 applications requesting more than $193 million during the 2026-2027 application period. DeSantis said the funding is part of broader hurricane recovery efforts and long-term economic strengthening for rural Florida communities.

item.content:encoded:

The figure represents the county's preliminary estimate of destruction from the hurricane. Local officials typically use damage assessments like this to help guide recovery priorities, apply for state and federal disaster aid, and plan rebuilding efforts.

The assessment comes as Escambia County and surrounding areas continue recovery operations in the wake of the storm.

item.title: Senator Moody introduces bill to protect anonymity in crime stoppers rewards
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Senator Ashley Moody rolled out new federal legislation today aimed at helping citizens report crimes while staying anonymous—even when collecting rewards for tips that lead to arrests. During a Crime Prevention Month event in Tampa, Moody gathered with law enforcement officials from across the Tampa Bay region, including Hillsborough County…
item.content:encoded:
Senator Ashley Moody rolled out new federal legislation today aimed at helping citizens report crimes while staying anonymous—even when collecting rewards for tips that lead to arrests.

During a Crime Prevention Month event in Tampa, Moody gathered with law enforcement officials from across the Tampa Bay region, including Hillsborough County Sheriff's Office deputies. She highlighted her push to empower ordinary people to assist police, building on what the FBI recently reported as a historic drop in violent crime nationwide.

"It's vital that citizens are empowered to help fight crime," Moody said, referencing her work creating Florida's **TIPS statewide tip hotline when she served as Attorney General. Her new bill, she said, would let people collect reward money for helping officers make arrests without having to give up their anonymity.

The legislation has backing from major law enforcement groups including the Florida Association of Crime Stoppers, Florida Sheriffs Association, the Southeastern Crime Stoppers Association, and the National Fraternal Order of Police. According to Crime Stoppers officials, the bill addresses a federal reporting requirement that can complicate anonymous cash reward payments—a challenge that's emerged over 50 years of operating tip programs across multiple states.

item.title: Santa Rosa Health Dept. Offers Walk-In Tetanus Shots Thursday
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Florida Department of Health in Santa Rosa County is hosting a walk-in tetanus vaccination clinic Thursday, October 15, from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. at their Milton office, 5527 Stewart St. No appointment is needed. The clinic comes as the region continues recovery efforts following recent hurricane activity. Tetanus, caused by bacteria found in soil…
item.content:encoded:
The Florida Department of Health in Santa Rosa County is hosting a walk-in tetanus vaccination clinic Thursday, October 15, from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. at their Milton office, 5527 Stewart St. No appointment is needed.

The clinic comes as the region continues recovery efforts following recent hurricane activity. Tetanus, caused by bacteria found in soil and the environment, can enter the body through wounds — particularly cuts from contaminated debris. The infection classically affects the jaw and neck muscles, leading to the common name "lockjaw." Hurricane cleanup work significantly increases exposure risk through minor cuts and puncture wounds that might otherwise go unnoticed.

Residents of Santa Rosa County who need a tetanus booster or primary vaccination are encouraged to attend. Those with questions about the tetanus vaccine can contact the health department at 850-851-8929 or visit the CDC's vaccine information page for more details.

item.content:encoded:
The City of Milton is hosting a community meal distribution event tonight to assist residents affected by Hurricane Isaias. The Jack Brewer Foundation will provide 1,000 prepared meals on a first-come, first-served basis beginning at 6 p.m. at Jernigan's Landing.

Each vehicle is limited to four meals, and distribution will continue while supplies last. The city has outlined a specific traffic route to manage the flow of vehicles: drivers should enter via Canal Street, continue to Pine Street, and proceed to Willing Street to access the pickup location. Personnel will be on hand to direct traffic and assist with the distribution.

For more information, residents can contact the City of Milton at (850) 983-5400.

item.content:encoded:
Rock band Matchbox Twenty is bringing their 30th Anniversary Tour to the Gulf Coast next summer. According to a Live Nation announcement, the group will perform at The Wharf Amphitheater in Orange Beach on August 5, 2027.

The tour marks a milestone year for the rock band, which formed in the mid-1990s and has built a devoted fanbase through hits like "3AM" and "Bent." Specific ticket information and on-sale dates have not yet been announced.

The Wharf Amphitheater is Orange Beach's premier outdoor music venue and regularly hosts major touring acts. More details about the concert are expected to be released by Live Nation in the coming weeks.

item.title: BRACE Seeks Donations for Long-Term Isaias Recovery in Escambia, Santa Rosa
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: PENSACOLA, Fla. — As Northwest Florida moves from emergency response into longer-term Hurricane Isaias recovery, BRACE is asking residents and businesses to help support recovery efforts in Escambia and Santa Rosa counties. Be Ready Alliance Coordinating for Emergencies serves as the lead local agency for Emergency Support Function 15, which…
item.content:encoded:
PENSACOLA, Fla. — As Northwest Florida moves from emergency response into longer-term Hurricane Isaias recovery, BRACE is asking residents and businesses to help support recovery efforts in Escambia and Santa Rosa counties.

Be Ready Alliance Coordinating for Emergencies serves as the lead local agency for Emergency Support Function 15, which coordinates volunteers and donations following disasters.

The organization also serves as a fiscal agent for disaster-recovery efforts in the two counties and leads their Long-Term Recovery Groups.

Those groups bring together nonprofit organizations, churches, businesses, government agencies and other community partners to address needs that can remain long after the immediate emergency ends.

“Disaster recovery does not end when the storm passes,” BRACE CEO Dr. Nick Jackson said. “Families may continue dealing with damaged homes, debris, lost belongings and other needs long after the immediate emergency is over.”

BRACE says financial contributions are particularly useful because recovery needs can change over time and funding can be directed toward identified gaps not covered by other resources.

Residents can contribute through the BRACE Hurricane Recovery donation page.

BRACE will continue coordinating with emergency managers in Escambia and Santa Rosa counties as recovery needs are identified.

item.title: Santa Rosa Expands Hurricane Supply Distribution; Six PODs Operating
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: SANTA ROSA COUNTY, Fla. — Santa Rosa County has expanded its Hurricane Isaias supply distribution operation, with six Points of Distribution now serving residents from Navarre to Jay. The newest locations are Navarre High School and Tiger Point Community Center in Gulf Breeze . Both are scheduled to operate from 7 a.m. until 7 p.m. daily until…
item.content:encoded:
SANTA ROSA COUNTY, Fla. — Santa Rosa County has expanded its Hurricane Isaias supply distribution operation, with six Points of Distribution now serving residents from Navarre to Jay.

The newest locations are Navarre High School and Tiger Point Community Center in Gulf Breeze.

Both are scheduled to operate from 7 a.m. until 7 p.m. daily until further notice, providing water, ice and tarps.

Four additional PODs are operating at Hickory Hammock Baptist Church in East Milton, Bray-Hendricks Park in Jay, King Middle School in Milton and Munson Air Strip.

The northern sites are distributing MREs, water, ice and tarps.

Additional feeding operations are also underway through the Red Cross, Salvation Army and other disaster-relief organizations.

Residents needing physical help cleaning up storm damage can also contact Crisis Cleanup at 800-451-1954.

Volunteer organizations may be able to assist with roof tarping, fallen-tree removal, debris cleanup and other storm-related needs. Assistance depends on volunteer availability.
